title: AI Prompting Power with Tomi Abe
description: Advanced prompting and generative workflow training for Loblaw Digital's AI Committee.
content:
In a webinar hosted by Loblaw Digital's AI Committee, I shared my strategies for using generative AI tools and strategic prompting techniques to elevate creative and design work. The session focused on bridging the gap between human intent and machine execution, demonstrating how non-creatives can unlock immense creative potential and how seasoned professionals can build custom design assets without losing their distinct craft or judgment.

Key highlights from the session:

  • The Three-Step Creative Process: I broke down my personal workflow for generating high-quality AI art, which relies heavily on upfront research and artistic insight to guide the visual direction, followed by strategic prompt writing and image generation.
  • Prompt Engineering with LLMs: I demonstrated how to strategically use language models like ChatGPT or Gemini to research cultural nuances and expand basic ideas into highly descriptive, detailed prompt frameworks.
  • Achieving Authenticity and Brand Consistency: We discussed how to overcome the typical "stiff" or "way too perfect" look of generic AI images. By specifying cinematic parameters—such as aspect ratios, specific film types (like CineStill film), color palettes, and framing—creatives can maintain a consistent visual aesthetic and direct complex lighting and emotions.
  • Live Midjourney Demonstration: The training featured a live look into Midjourney via Discord, illustrating the progression from basic prompts to highly stylized landscape images. I also demonstrated Midjourney's /describe feature, showing how to upload an existing image to reverse-engineer descriptive prompts and establish a stylistic baseline.
  • Ethics and Limitations: The session concluded with a discussion on ethical boundaries in AI art, highlighting the importance of avoiding the direct replication of existing artists' styles to respect copyright compliance. We also addressed current technical limitations, noting that generated imagery functions well as custom editorial support but cannot yet be exported directly as editable vector files for tools like Illustrator.
